questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
It was important to me, that the university offered courses in physical geography and geoinformatics, and in particular, that it was recommended by former students. It was also important, that I would be able to understand the language in what they would be teaching.
I also contacted the university early on to hear about their module offers, as I had questions to what the possibilities were regarding master modules and also just guidance. They were very kind, and helped as much as they could remotely.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been great to experience something else. The situation with Covid-19 has been inconvenient anyway, even though we hoped for it to be different this year. I had hoped to have more face-to-face teaching and possibilities to engage with students from England. I also had an annoying experience with the student service. At least I had the opportunity to meet a lot of great people, both locals and other international students! These will definitely be there for life!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It took some time for them to confirm a recommended date of arrival. That was inconvenient, as you want to book tickets as soon as possible. Otherwise I has good information about contacts in my parent school and the student service and the student union, but for my accomodation, I got information about key pick-up on the day I arrived!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to another accomodation reception to pick up my keys.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was loads of information, but there was too much, and much information was not even relevant to me as an international student. Also, it would have helped to have had the meeting for erasmus students at the beginning of the first week, instead of in the end. Then, we could have been guided to the vital parts of the freshers week at out parent school.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was through the host institution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Get a bike. It's faster, cheaper, you get a bit of exercise, and you have a lot more freedom. Also, it's more peaceful to live further away from campus. Also mentally!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accomodation is a bit worn down, but it's good for the price, and the staff were very kind and helpful.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was sad, that they changed the semester for the one module, that I almost picked the university for.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You wish for modules worth more credits than you can have. Then they assess whether or not you are qualified for these modules, and enroll you in all modules they think you qualify for. Before semesterstart, you will have to either enroll in more modules in order to have enough credits or deregister for some modules - perhaps some of them are at the same time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A module catalogue and the student service at my parent school-

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got registered in all modules I wanted, even though not all first priorities.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make your research on avaliable modules and be open-minded, as you will have to choose from last years module catalogue. Also, be aware of what modules you get enrolled in, so you can change or deselect or select more modules if needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
Corona happened. I had a lot of self-studies - reading, youtube-videoes, searching on topics on my own, tasks and so on. I think they did an ok job at not making it too similar all the time.
I was not satisfied with the distribution of assignments throughout the semester, and the student service wouldn't help me, even though they couldn't find due dates for 3 assignments.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It varies a lot. The two modules in which had to work hardest was a master module and level 1 module. I would say the level 1 module was not proportional for it's level, otherwise it should have been worth more credits.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It's hard to tell, as I didn't get to have much teaching due to corona. I had one in-person seminar, one in-person lecture and one online lecture. They used self-studies more than at UCPH. The style of teaching is somewhat similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Programming for the Web
Traditional Alcoholic Beverages
Glacial Landforms and Processes
Creating Alternative Futures
GIS and Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Creating Alternative Futures is highly recommended, as you engage in a critical discussion of society, and think about alternatives in a world of change. This is about socialism, civil empowerment and structures of power and how to change them. 
GIS and Environment is great for practising your GIS-skills and develop your knowledge on physical geography and mapping.
These are really good modules, where you gain in-depth knowledge on the topic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The socities at uni have different prices for memberships

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: You just end up spending a lot of money on being with new friends and buying a bit of stuff for you to bring back.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of socities! Almost anything you can think of.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything...

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Darts! It's a lot of fun and the society is festive and everyone loves to drink a pint while playing. This is an authentic experience, and do yourself a favour and play in a tournament! It's truly one of my best memories, especially the bus drive home. It was just english chants and songs all the way.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go hikinh in the countryside. Also visit some major cities, Liverpool and Manchester are not far away, and York is a great place with a lot of history. Especially at christmas!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Dart society!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They party culture.. English people can behave really rude when drunk.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Involve yourself in a society, participate in the icebreaker activities before the semester starts and get there early.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: All lectures and seminars end before christmas. Plan early what you want to do for christmas and new year's, a lot of people want to stay, but everyone is afraid no one is there, so make arrangements early on before people buy tickets home.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting locals and learning about cultures through other international students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had a lot of assements due within the same 3 weeks, which made it hard to actually gain in-depth knowledge. I just had to make it through.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange! It is such a good experience, and you learn a lot about yourself when you are challenged to establish in a foreign country.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
